text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Ruling coalition supports Finance Minister Theo Waigel to defeat opposition parliamentary motion calling for him to be sacked, as Waigel defends his plans to revalue Bundesbank gold.
- German Aerospace industry threatens to call off preparations for Eurofighter project if Bonn doesn't approve it soon. Defence Minister Volker Ruehe confident it will go ahead.
- German prosecutors demand acquittal for a Lebanese man charged with starting a fire last year that killed 10 people.
- One man dies and many injured in fire at asylum seekers' hostel. Arson and racist motives not being ruled out.

- German chemical industry becomes first sector to make its wage bargaining process more flexible, allowing wages to be decreased by up to 10 percent in times of economic difficulty or for competitive reasons.
- Bonn and Germany's 16 federal states want to launch advertising campaign to promote Germany as a place to do business.
HANDELSBLATT
- Finance Minister Waigel wants to put on the spending brakes to help solve budget crisis.
- Coalition backs Waigel in parliamentary vote.
- Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG ready to put up a missing one billion marks to secure Bonn's approval of the Eurofighter project.
- Economy in west Germany picks up significantly according to the Handlesblatt early indicator for June, showing growth rising 0.3 percent this month to an annual 1.9 percent.
- General secretary of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) Renato Ruggiero says Germany has important role to play in promoting mulitlateral trade policies.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Waigel announces spending freeze for 1997 to help budget woes.

- Gerhard Schroeder, a leading opposition Social Democrats (SPD) potential candidate for chancellor, was quoted in an article as saying he believed it would be better to delay the launch of Europe's planned single currency than to soften the criteria.
- State prosecutor recommends acquittal for arson suspect.
DIE WELT
- Opposition motion calling for sacking of Waigel fails as the finance minister calls for spending freeze.
- Leading economists warn Bonn against accounting tricks to qualify for Europe's single currency.
- Aerospace puts pressure on Bonn to approve Eurofighter project.
- Prosecutor calls for acquittal for Lebanese arson suspect.
